name: comp-264
title: Object Position Slider
description: A position panel with one slider and one small number box per axis. X, Y and Z can be dragged or typed, and a Reset button puts all three back to zero.
use: An editor needs to nudge an object on three axes and also type exact coordinates.
avoid: A single free 2D drag area is wanted; here each axis is its own separate row.
a11y: The sliders are named X, Y and Z, but every number box is called Enter value, so they cannot be told apart. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: The heading Object position sits over three rows, each starting with a small grey letter, then a grey track with a white fill and round knob, then a narrow rounded box holding a number. A full-width outlined Reset button with a circular arrow closes the group.
behaves: Dragging a knob shifts that axis and rewrites its box, while typing a number and confirming jumps the knob to match. Reset snaps X, Y and Z back to zero together.
customise: Axis names, the minus ten to ten range, starting values and the reset target are written in the source; adding an axis means another block.
weight: light: Three small sliders, three inputs and a button; idle until touched.
